title: Governance Gate Decision Spine v1 — Implementation Plan
summary: Phased implementation plan to wire canonical governance gate decision events (rig.relay.governance.gate.decision) across all 22 governance gates, with classification into six decision outcomes and four test classifications.

sections.content: Governance Gate Decision Spine — Implementation Plan

Use one canonical event (rig.relay.governance.gate.decision) with a decision field carrying one of six outcomes. Do NOT create paired event names (allow/block). This aligns with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions, OWASP security logging guidance, and NIST SP 800-92.
Phase 0: Schema + Emitter + Golden DuckDB Test

Add rig.relay.governance_gate_decision.v1 schema. Add emit_governance_gate_decision() function — not send_governance_gate_decision() that chooses between separate event names. Write one golden DuckDB projection test that proves the event shape is groupable by gate, decision, reason, tool_name, and severity.

Crypto gaps are not Phase 4 polish — they are Phase 1. If the local action envelope silently returns False on signature failure, payload hash mismatch, or replay expiry, that is missing security audit evidence at the boundary where Rig claims to be governed.

Emitter helper enum/field validation. Decision enum stability. Reason code format.
JSON schema validation for rig.relay.governance_gate_decision.v1. Content-light invariant holds. additionalProperties rejected.
Tool runtime paths emit exactly one decision event per gate per invocation. All six decision classes reachable.
JSONL telemetry files are written and DuckDB-groupable. Schema-validated artifacts exist on disk.

Cryptographic mismatch emits failed_closed. Expired envelope emits failed_closed. Missing policy object emits failed_closed with operator_action_required=true. Dev bypass emits allowed with severity=warning.
DuckDB projection over JSONL proves: group by gate, decision, reason, tool_name; count per severity; trending per policy_version.
